_README: Bali fact layer, built 2026-10-13. Every row's source_url was opened and read on checked_at. Most rows are primary; a few are marked source_kind 'secondary' where no official page could be reached, and each of those says why in its caveat, and 'support' quotes what the page said. Consensus-only, secondary and unsourced material deliberately did NOT make it in; it stays in raw/claude.json (_open_questions) and disputes.md. An absent fact means 'not proven', never 'not true'. serve_live values (exchange rates, prices, flight times, budgets) are intentionally absent. Rupiah amounts are regulation figures; never freeze a dollar equivalent beside them.

_meta.review_status: PROMOTED 2026-10-13. The user delegated verification to Claude ('if you can't find it in Google or by yourself, I can't check it too'); every record was read on its source page by Claude on checked_at.
_meta.built_from: raw/claude.json + raw/chatgpt.json + raw/deepseek.json, reconciled; drafted by Claude from primary pages it opened itself
deliberately_excluded: ATM limits and fees, service-charge percentages, tipping amounts
all recommendations and itineraries (they live in the candidates file, not here)
seasonal rainfall figures - the weather agency publishes year-specific forecasts, not an evergreen statement
whether an international permit must itself be endorsed for motorcycles - the statute sets the licence-class rule but does not mention permits by category
door-to-door flight times from US airports and which hubs connect - schedule data, serve live

fast-boat safety and Sanur harbour closures: the Transport Ministry's own post on the August 2025 fast-boat capsizing exists but its site rejected every request, and the one news report tried returned 403; only search snippets were seen (harbour closed 6 August 2025 for bad weather after the accident), so nothing was stored
fast-boat operators, harbours per operator, refund practice - seller pages only

_human_checklist: All five review items from the first draft were closed by Claude on 2026-10-13 by re-reading the pages directly (CDC, Bank Indonesia, State Dept) and by fixing wording rules into the records (writing_rule fields).
Residual: Nyepi airport closure hours (news quote only); Galungan/Kuningan 2027 held as secondary until the ministry PDF can be opened.

timezones.value: Indonesia has 3 time zones and does not observe daylight saving time. Jakarta, in the western zone, is 12 hours ahead of Washington DC during Eastern Standard Time.
timezones.scope: Indonesia; the page gives the gap for Jakarta, not Bali
timezones.support: State Dept, read directly: 'There are 3 time zones, and the main time zone is Western Indonesia Time. It does not observe daylight saving time. Jakarta is 12 hours ahead of Washington D.C. during Eastern Standard Time.'
timezones.writing_rule: Bali is in the central zone, one hour ahead of Jakarta - stable geography, not stated on this page. Compute US gaps from UTC+8 at write time; because the US changes clocks and Bali does not, the gap shifts by an hour twice a year.

type.value: A visa is required. A US passport holder can get the B1 Tourist visa either online in advance (the e-VOA) or on arrival at the airport, where queues can be long.
type.scope: US ordinary passport holders visiting Bali as tourists
type.support: State Dept: 'A visa is required.' 'You can apply for a 30-day electronic visa in advance if arriving at airports in Jakarta or Bali.' 'You can purchase a visa upon arrival at the airport. You may need to wait in long lines, and the process may take longer.' Official visa finder lists 'B1 - Tourist (Visa On Arrival)' for UNITED STATES OF AMERICA.

fee.scope: US ordinary passport holders visiting Bali as tourists
fee.support: Ngurah Rai immigration office: 'Biaya Visa Kunjungan Saat Kedatangan sebesar Rp 500.000,-' and lists Amerika Serikat among eligible countries. Official e-visa finder (US passport > Tourism > B1): 'Cost: Rp500.000'.

check_candidate.pattern: Biaya Visa Kunjungan Saat Kedatangan sebesar Rp\s*([0-9.]+)
check_candidate.note: proposal only; not a registered check config

fee.display_rule: rupiah only; any dollar equivalent is serve_live

max_stay_days.value: 30 days, extendable once for another 30 days
max_stay_days.scope: US ordinary passport holders visiting Bali as tourists
max_stay_days.support: Official e-visa finder, B1: 'Stay: Up to 30 days (extendable for another 30 days)'. Ngurah Rai immigration office: 30 days, 'dapat diperpanjang 1 (satu) kali pada Kantor Imigrasi'.

validity_to_enter.value: The visa is valid for 90 days from issue; apply and pay within 90 days of arrival.
validity_to_enter.scope: US ordinary passport holders visiting Bali as tourists
validity_to_enter.support: Official e-visa finder, B1: 'Visa Validity: 90 day'. State Dept: 'Within 90 days of arrival: Apply and pay for an e-visa online through https://evisa.imigrasi.go.id/.'

official_application_site.value: https://evisa.imigrasi.go.id/ is the official e-visa site (Directorate General of Immigration). Payment is by Mastercard, Visa or JCB card; one application can cover up to 5 people.
official_application_site.scope: US ordinary passport holders visiting Bali as tourists
official_application_site.support: Homepage: 'The Official e-Visa Website for Indonesia'; 'Make Visa fee payment by SIMPONI or Mastercard, Visa or JCB credit/debit card'; 'Electronic Visa on Arrival (e-VOA) application can be done simultaneously for 5 people'. The same URL is printed on the State Dept page.

arrival_card.value: Separate from the visa, every traveler must submit an arrival card through the All Indonesia system. It can only be completed within 72 hours (3 days) before arrival, it is free, and it produces a QR code to show Immigration and Customs.
arrival_card.scope: all international passengers arriving in Indonesia
arrival_card.support: State Dept: 'Complete an arrival card online or through the All Indonesia mobile app. The website will not allow you to complete the arrival card if you attempt to complete it more than 72 hours prior to your arrival. Save the QR code... This service is completely free.' E-visa homepage: 'All travellers are required to submit an arrival card within 3 (three) days prior arrival in Indonesia'.
arrival_card.writing_rule: Tell readers to complete it during the last two days before arrival: that satisfies both the 72-hour limit (State Dept, e-visa site) and customs' two-day window, so the disagreement never reaches the reader.

tourist_levy.value: Foreign tourists entering Bali pay a tourist levy of IDR 150,000 per person. It is separate from the visa and can be paid cashless online before travel or at counters at Bali's airport and seaport; proof is a QR voucher sent by email.
tourist_levy.support: State Dept: 'Foreign tourists entering Bali must pay a tourist levy of IDR 150,000 per person. The tourist levy is separate from the e-VOA or the Visa on Arrival. Cashless payments can be made online before your travel or on arrival at designated payment counters at Bali's airport and seaport.' Provincial site lovebali.baliprov.go.id shows 'IDR 150,000' and 'Your Levy Voucher will be sent to your Email'.

overstay_penalty.value: Overstaying, or entering on the wrong visa type, can bring a fine of IDR 1,000,000 per day, plus possible detention, deportation or a ban on returning.
overstay_penalty.scope: US ordinary passport holders visiting Bali as tourists
overstay_penalty.support: State Dept: 'If you enter Indonesia with the wrong type of visa or if you overstay your visa, you may be fined 1,000,000 rupiah per day. You may also face detention, deportation, or not be allowed to come back.'

activities_allowed.value: The B1 visa covers tourism and visiting friends or family, business meetings and site visits, and medical treatment. It does not allow selling goods or services or being paid by anyone in Indonesia.
activities_allowed.scope: US ordinary passport holders visiting Bali as tourists
activities_allowed.support: Official e-visa finder, B1: 'You are prohibited from selling goods or services. You are prohibited from receiving rewards or wages from individuals or companies in Indonesia.'

tourist_levy_terms.value: The Bali tourist levy is paid once per trip, before the traveler leaves Indonesia, and only cashless: online in advance, at counters at Bali's airport and port, or through registered hotels, travel agents and attractions. Accepted: Visa, Mastercard, American Express and JCB cards, bank transfer, virtual account, UnionPay and QRIS. Proof is a voucher with a QR code sent by email. Cruise passengers pay too.
tourist_levy_terms.support: Love Bali FAQ, read directly: 'The levy is paid only 1 (one) time while traveling in Bali, before the person leaves the territory of the Republic of Indonesia.' 'Payment must be done cashless through electronic payment facilities.' 'Yes, this tax applies to cruise passengers.'

tourist_levy_exemptions.value: Exempt from the levy: holders of diplomatic and official visas, transport crew, holders of temporary or permanent stay permits (KITAS/KITAP), and holders of family unification, student, golden and certain other visas. Golden-visa and 'other visa' holders must apply through the Love Bali system; the rest show their card to the officer. An ordinary tourist on a visa on arrival is not exempt.
tourist_levy_exemptions.support: Love Bali FAQ, read directly: 'Exemptions are granted to: (a) Holders of diplomatic and official visas; (b) Crew members on transportation vehicles; (c) Holder of Temporary Stay Permit Card (KITAS) or Permanent Stay Permit Card (KITAP); (d) Holders of Family unification visas; (e) Holders of Student visas; (f) Holders of Golden visas, and (g) Holders of other visas. Points (f) and (g) need to apply through the Love Bali system'. Legal basis listed: Law 15/2023 on Bali Province; Provincial Regulation 2/2025 amending 6/2023; Governor Regulation 25/2025; Governor Decree 699/03-L/HK/2025.
tourist_levy_exemptions.writing_rule: The last sentence of the value is an inference from the list (no tourist-visa category appears in it), not a quoted line.

tourist_levy_enforcement.value: Under the Bali governor's 2025 circular, a foreign tourist who has not paid the levy is refused service at tourist attractions.
tourist_levy_enforcement.support: Bali provincial media centre, 24 March 2025, on Circular (SE) No. 7 of 2025: 'Turis yang belum membayar Pungutan Wisatawan Asing dikenakan sanksi tidak mendapatkan pelayanan di Daya Tarik Wisata.'

extension_fee.value: Extending the stay for another 30 days costs IDR 500,000 per application, the official fee for a visit stay permit of up to 30 days.
extension_fee.scope: US tourists extending a 30-day visa on arrival
extension_fee.support: Directorate General of Immigration fee table, read directly: 'Izin Tinggal Kunjungan Masa Berlaku Paling lama 30 Hari per Permohonan Rp 500.000,-'. Two immigration offices' own pages, seen in Google results but not opened (certificate and redirect errors), word it as a VoA extension: Singaraja (Bali) 'Perpanjangan Visa on Arrival (VoA) berlaku 30 (tiga puluh) Hari Rp. 500.000,-'; Manado 'Rp 500.000,- per permohonan'.
extension_fee.caveat: The fee table names the permit class, not 'VoA extension' in so many words; the link to VoA rests on the two office pages seen only as search snippets. Whether a visa bought at the airport counter can be extended online is still not sourced.

extension_process.value: A visa on arrival, whether bought online (e-VOA) or as a sticker at the airport counter, is extended by applying and paying online at evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Since 29 May 2025 the applicant must then go to an immigration office for a photograph and an interview. Applying and paying before the visa expires means no overstay is charged while the application is processed.
extension_process.scope: foreign visitors extending a visa on arrival in Indonesia
extension_process.support: Directorate General of Immigration press release, 28 May 2025, read directly in Chrome: 'Mengacu pada Surat Edaran Nomor IMI-417.GR.01.01 Tahun 2025, yang akan berlaku efektif mulai 29 Mei 2025, WNA di Indonesia wajib melakukan pengambilan foto dan wawancara di kantor imigrasi saat mengajukan perpanjangan izin tinggal. Sebelum tahapan tersebut, WNA mendaftar permohonan izin tinggal dan mengunggah dokumen persyaratan secara online melalui website evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Prosedur ini juga berlaku bagi WNA pemegang visa on arrival (VoA).' Vulnerable groups (elderly, disabled, pregnant or nursing, urgent cases) may do everything walk-in. Immigration news item, 8 Nov 2024, read directly: online extension is open 'baik bagi WNA yang menggunakan VoA elektronik (e-VoA) maupun VoA berbentuk stiker yang didapatkan di konter imigrasi area kedatangan bandara'; e-VOA holders use 'Extend My Visa', airport-sticker holders use Services > 'Find Existing Stay Permit'; payment by Visa/Mastercard debit or credit card; 'WNA tidak akan dikenakan overstay apabila pengajuan dan pembayaran perpanjangan VoA ... dilakukan sebelum masa berlaku visa berakhir' (Permenkumham 11/2024 art. 97); verification is by the immigration office for the foreigner's place of stay.
extension_process.caveat: Processing time is not stated by either source; never print a number of days. Which office handles a given address is not listed in the sources.
extension_process.writing_rule: Say both visa versions extend the same way: online application, then an in-person photo and interview. Do not say the e-VOA extends without a visit (true in 2023, superseded).

passport_validity.value: The passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond the arrival date and have 2 blank pages. The endorsement page at the back does not count as blank. Travelers who do not meet this are refused entry.
passport_validity.scope: US ordinary passport holders visiting Bali as tourists
passport_validity.support: US Consular Agency Bali: 'All visitors to Bali must have passports that have at least six months of validity and have two blank passport pages. The "endorsement" page at the back of the passport does not count as a blank page. Balinese immigration authorities will not allow you to enter the country if you do not meet this requirement.' State Dept: 'Must have 6 months validity beyond your arrival date. 2 blank pages required for entry.'

onward_ticket.value: An outbound ticket from Indonesia is one of the documents to present to the immigration officer on arrival.
onward_ticket.scope: US ordinary passport holders visiting Bali as tourists
onward_ticket.support: Official e-visa finder, B1, Document Requirement: 'Present the following documents to the immigration officer upon arrival for immigration inspection: Passport valid for at least 6 months. Outbound ticket from Indonesia.'

emergency_passport.value: A traveler on a limited-validity (emergency) passport needs a visa obtained before arrival from an Indonesian embassy or consulate; the visa on arrival is not available.
emergency_passport.scope: US citizens traveling on an emergency passport
emergency_passport.support: US Consular Agency Bali: 'If you are traveling on a limited-validity (i.e. emergency) passport, you will require a visa prior to arriving in Indonesia.'

same_passport_exit.value: You must leave Indonesia on the same passport you entered with. If it is replaced during the trip, a 'special pass' from immigration is needed before departure.
same_passport_exit.scope: US ordinary passport holders visiting Bali as tourists
same_passport_exit.support: State Dept: 'You must exit Indonesia with the same passport you used to enter. If your passport is replaced, you must obtain a "special pass" from immigration authorities before leaving.'

cash_declaration.value: Cash or other payment instruments worth IDR 100,000,000 or more, in rupiah or foreign currency, must be declared to Customs when entering or leaving. It is a declaration duty, not a cap. Failing to declare carries a penalty of 10% of the amount, capped at IDR 300,000,000.
cash_declaration.scope: all international passengers arriving in Indonesia
cash_declaration.support: Customs FAQ: 'Pembawaan Uang Tunai dan/atau Instrumen Pembayaran Lain dengan nilai paling sedikit Rp100.000.000,00 (seratus juta Rupiah) wajib diberitahukan kepada Pejabat Bea dan Cukai'; 'sanksi administrasi sebesar 10% dari seluruh jumlah uang tunai ... paling banyak Rp300.000.000,00' (PMK 100/PMK.04/2018).
cash_declaration.caveat: The State Dept page words this as an 'Entry maximum / Exit maximum'; Customs is the competent source.

rupiah_export_permit.value: Taking IDR 100,000,000 or more in rupiah out of Indonesia requires a permit from Bank Indonesia. An individual may not carry foreign banknotes worth IDR 1,000,000,000 or more.
rupiah_export_permit.scope: all international passengers arriving in Indonesia
rupiah_export_permit.support: Customs FAQ: 'Pembawaan uang tunai dengan mata uang rupiah paling sedikit Rp100.000.000,00 ... keluar daerah pabean indonesia wajib mendapat izin dari Bank Indonesia'; 'Orang perseorangan dilarang melakukan pembawaan uang tunai berupa Uang Kertas Asing dengan nilai paling sedikit setara dengan Rp1.000.000.000,00'.

duty_free_goods_value.value: Personal goods worth up to USD 500 per person per arrival enter free of import duty and tax. The excess is charged 10% import duty plus VAT.
duty_free_goods_value.scope: all international passengers arriving in Indonesia
duty_free_goods_value.support: Customs: 'barang pribadi Penumpang umum dengan nilai pabean paling banyak USD 500 per orang untuk setiap kedatangan, diberikan pembebasan Bea Masuk'; 'atas kelebihan tersebut dipungut bea masuk sebesar 10% dan PPN'.
duty_free_goods_value.display_rule: USD 500 is the regulation's own figure, not a conversion

alcohol_allowance.value: Up to 1 liter of alcoholic drink per adult passenger aged 21 or over.
alcohol_allowance.scope: all international passengers arriving in Indonesia
alcohol_allowance.support: Customs: 'untuk minuman yang mengandung etil alkohol, diberikan paling banyak 1 (satu) liter untuk penumpang berusia 21 tahun ke atas'.

tobacco_allowance.value: 200 cigarettes, or 25 cigars, or 100 grams of sliced or other tobacco per adult passenger; mixed types are pro-rated.
tobacco_allowance.scope: all international passengers arriving in Indonesia
tobacco_allowance.support: Customs: 'sigaret, diberikan paling banyak 200 (dua ratus) batang; cerutu ... 25 ... batang; tembakau iris ... 100 (seratus) gram'.

vape_allowance.value: E-cigarette allowance for passengers aged 18 or over: 30 ml of open-system liquid, or 12 ml of closed-system liquid, or 140 sticks / 40 capsules of solid product.
vape_allowance.scope: all international passengers arriving in Indonesia
vape_allowance.support: Customs: 'rokok elektrik padat ... 140 batang atau 40 kapsul; rokok elektrik cair sistem terbuka ... 30 mililiter; rokok elektrik cair sistem tertutup ... 12 mililiter, untuk penumpang berusia 18 tahun ke atas'.

excess_destroyed.value: Alcohol, tobacco or vape products above the allowance are destroyed on the spot by the customs officer; they are not taxed and released.
excess_destroyed.scope: all international passengers arriving in Indonesia
excess_destroyed.support: Customs: 'atas kelebihan jumlah tersebut langsung dimusnahkan oleh Pejabat Bea dan Cukai dengan atau tanpa disaksikan Penumpang'.

medicines_inspected.value: Medicines are on the list of items that send a passenger to the red (inspection) channel, alongside animal and plant products, goods above the duty-free value, and large amounts of cash.
medicines_inspected.scope: all international passengers arriving in Indonesia
medicines_inspected.support: Customs, Jalur Merah list: 'narkotika, psikotropika, prekursor, obat-obatan, senjata api...'

medication_import.value: Medicine for personal use in a passenger's own baggage needs no agency approval, but every medicine brought from abroad must be backed by a doctor's prescription or hospital recommendation, for at most 90 days' use, with a special form and supporting documents. Over-the-counter medicines may come in without a prescription for at most 3 days' need. Psychotropic medicines are allowed for at most 60 days' need. Narcotic-class medicines and precursors may not be brought in at all. Medicine that does not comply can be seized and destroyed.
medication_import.scope: all international passengers arriving in Indonesia
medication_import.support: BPOM FAQ: 'Obat untuk tujuan penggunaan pribadi tidak memerlukan persetujuan dari BPOM maupun Kementerian Kesehatan, pemohon hanya diminta mengisi Formulir Khusus dan melampirkan dokumen yang dipersyaratkan untuk penggunaan maksimal 90 hari (3 bulan); Seluruh jenis obat yang dibawa dari luar negeri harus berdasarkan resep dokter atau rekomendasi rumah sakit; ... Obat Bebas ... tanpa resep dokter untuk kebutuhan maksimal 3 hari; Obat golongan Narkotika dan Prekursor tidak diperkenankan dibawa dari luar negeri; dan Obat golongan Psikotropika ... maksimal 60 hari (2 bulan).'
medication_import.writing_rule: Give the rule by class exactly as BPOM states it. Name no drug as allowed or banned, with one exception: the State Dept says ADHD medications are illegal. Tell readers to check their own medication's class and to carry the prescription; point to the BPOM contact for individual cases.

drug_laws.value: Marijuana, cannabis and CBD products are illegal in Indonesia. Some prescription medications, including those for ADHD, are illegal, and customs does not publish a list of prohibited drugs. Convictions can bring heavy fines and long jail sentences, and in extreme cases the death penalty.
drug_laws.scope: US ordinary passport holders visiting Bali as tourists
drug_laws.support: State Dept: 'Marijuana, cannabis, CBD products, and some prescription medications, including those for ADHD, are illegal in Indonesia. The Indonesian customs office does not share a list of prohibited drugs. Criminal convictions may result in heavy fines and long jail sentences. In extreme cases, the death penalty may apply.'

advisory_level.value: US State Department Travel Advisory for Indonesia: Level 2, Exercise increased caution, citing natural disasters, unrest and terrorism. The Level 4 'Do not travel' warning applies only to Central Papua and Highland Papua, not Bali.
advisory_level.support: State Dept: 'Level 2 - Exercise increased caution ... Date issued: July 07, 2026'; 'Do not travel to the provinces of Central Papua ... and Highland Papua ... due to civil unrest.'

drink_safety.value: The State Department warns of drink poisoning in Indonesia, including alcohol mixed with methanol, and reports drink spiking and sexual assault in Bali, Lombok and the Gili Islands. Its advice: watch drinks being prepared, never accept drinks from strangers, never leave a drink unattended.
drink_safety.scope: US ordinary passport holders visiting Bali as tourists
drink_safety.support: State Dept: 'Drink poisoning, like alcohol mixed with methanol or other deadly chemicals. Sexual assault and drink spiking have been reported in Bali, Lombok, Gili Islands, and Sumatra. Ensure drinks are prepared in your sight.'

vaccines.value: No vaccinations are required to enter Indonesia. The CDC recommends that travelers be current on routine vaccines and recommends hepatitis A, hepatitis B and typhoid; rabies and Japanese encephalitis vaccination depend on the trip.
vaccines.support: State Dept: 'No vaccinations are required.' CDC page read directly in a browser: Hepatitis A 'Recommended for unvaccinated travelers one year old or older going to Indonesia.' Hepatitis B 'Recommended for unvaccinated travelers of all ages traveling to Indonesia.' Typhoid 'Recommended for most travelers.' Japanese encephalitis 'Recommended for travelers who... spend long periods of time, such as a month or more, in areas with Japanese encephalitis'. Yellow fever: 'Vaccine is not recommended.'

malaria.value: The CDC reports no malaria transmission in the resort areas of Bali, in Ubud, or in the Gili Islands.
malaria.scope: travelers staying in Bali resort areas, Ubud and the Gili Islands
malaria.support: CDC, read directly: 'No malaria transmission in the cities of Jakarta (the capital) or Ubud'; 'No malaria transmission in the resort areas of Bali or Java, the Gili Islands, or the Thousand Islands (Pulau Seribu)'. Malaria block 'Updated April 23, 2025'.

rabies.value: The CDC says dogs infected with rabies are commonly found in Indonesia, that rabies vaccines are typically available throughout most of the country after an exposure, and that whether to get vaccinated before travel depends on planned activities and on how quickly a traveler could reach post-exposure treatment.
rabies.support: CDC, read directly: 'Dogs infected with rabies are commonly found in Indonesia. If rabies exposures occur while in Indonesia, rabies vaccines are typically available throughout most of the country. Rabies pre-exposure vaccination considerations include whether travelers 1) will be performing occupational or recreational activities that increase risk for exposure to potentially rabid animals and 2) might have difficulty getting prompt access to safe post-exposure prophylaxis.'

emergency_numbers.value: Emergency numbers in Bali's Badung regency: 112 (free unified emergency line), 110 police, 119 ambulance, 113 fire, 115 search and rescue.
emergency_numbers.scope: Badung regency, Bali (Kuta, Seminyak, Canggu, Jimbaran, the Bukit); the short codes are national
emergency_numbers.support: Badung communications office: 'Kepolisian = 110, Pemadam Kebakaran = 113, Basarnas = 115, Ambulan/Kemenkes = 119'; national 112 page: 'nomor darurat tunggal ... dapat dihubungi saat ponsel terkunci/tanpa pulsa (gratis)'.

us_consular_agency_bali.value: U.S. Consular Agency Bali: Jimbaran Hub, Jalan Karangmas, Jimbaran, Badung, Bali 80362. Phone +62-361-233-605. After-hours emergency +62-21-5083-1000, press 0 for the operator. Email CABali@state.gov.
us_consular_agency_bali.support: State Dept 'Embassies and consulates' block, verbatim address, phone and email.

enforcement_campaign.value: The US Consular Agency in Bali reports a current enforcement campaign by Indonesian police, immigration, transport and tourism officials, with stepped-up enforcement of traffic and vehicle violations, illegal work and other visa violations, and drug possession.
enforcement_campaign.support: Consular Agency page: 'U.S. citizens in Bali should be aware of a current enforcement campaign by the Indonesian authorities... resulting in increased enforcement of traffic and vehicle violations, illegal work or other visa violations, illegal drug possession and other crimes.'

zika_notice.value: The CDC has a Level 2 (Practice Enhanced Precautions) travel health notice for Zika in Indonesia, dated August 7, 2026: cases are being reported in travelers returning from Bali, and all travelers to Bali should take steps to prevent mosquito bites and sexual transmission during and after travel.
zika_notice.support: CDC, read directly: 'Level 2 Practice Enhanced Precautions - Zika in Indonesia - August 07, 2026 - Cases of Zika are being reported in returning travelers from Bali, Indonesia. All travelers to Bali should take steps to prevent mosquito bites and sexual transmission of Zika virus during and after travel.'
zika_notice.writing_rule: A live health notice: re-open before every batch that mentions it; matters most to anyone pregnant or planning pregnancy.

narcotics_law_penalties.value: Under Indonesia's Narcotics Law, cannabis and all parts and products of the plant are Class I narcotics. Unlawful possession of a Class I narcotic carries 4 to 12 years in prison and a fine of IDR 800 million to IDR 8 billion; importing one carries 5 to 15 years, and above 1 kilogram of plant material or 5 grams of other forms the penalty can be death or life imprisonment. Personal use of a Class I narcotic carries up to 4 years.
narcotics_law_penalties.support: Law 35 of 2009 on Narcotics, Health Ministry copy, text extracted and read: Pasal 111(1) and 112(1) 'pidana penjara paling singkat 4 (empat) tahun dan paling lama 12 (dua belas) tahun dan pidana denda paling sedikit Rp800.000.000,00 ... paling banyak Rp8.000.000.000,00'; Pasal 113(1) import/export 'paling singkat 5 (lima) tahun dan paling lama 15 (lima belas) tahun'; 113(2) 'melebihi 1 (satu) kilogram atau melebihi 5 (lima) batang pohon atau dalam bentuk bukan tanaman beratnya melebihi 5 (lima) gram, pelaku dipidana dengan pidana mati, pidana penjara seumur hidup, atau pidana penjara paling singkat 5 ... paling lama 20'; Pasal 127(1)(a) 'Narkotika Golongan I bagi diri sendiri dipidana dengan pidana penjara paling lama 4 (empat) tahun'; Annex, Golongan I no. 8 'Tanaman ganja, semua tanaman genus cannabis dan semua bagian dari tanaman ... termasuk damar ganja dan hasis', no. 9 Tetrahydrocannabinol.
narcotics_law_penalties.caveat: Statute as enacted in 2009; later amendments or the new criminal code were not checked. State the ranges as what the Narcotics Law provides, not as what a court will impose. The law does not mention CBD by name; that comes from the State Dept.

methanol_poisoning.value: Methanol is a toxic byproduct of alcohol production that can remain in a drink after improper distillation, and it is sometimes used to adulterate drinks in place of ethanol. It can cause dizziness, headache, nausea, permanent loss of vision, organ failure and death. Symptoms may not appear for 1 to 72 hours. The CDC advises travelers to choose reputable brands and drink in moderation.
methanol_poisoning.support: CDC Yellow Book: 'Methanol, a toxic byproduct of ethanol production, is normally eliminated in commercial products but with improper distillation can remain (or even become more concentrated) in the final product.' 'Methanol is also sometimes used to adulterate beverages in place of ethanol.' 'Methanol consumption can lead to dizziness, headache, nausea, permanent visual loss, organ failure, and death.' 'Advise travelers about the risks of consuming alcohol abroad, to only select reputable brands, and to drink in moderation.' CDC/NIOSH methanol card: 'Colorless watery liquid'; 'may not become apparent until after an asymptomatic period of 1 to 72 hours'; early effects 'drowsiness ... confusion, headache, dizziness'; 'blurred vision ... partial to total loss of vision'; 'Fomepizole and ethanol are effective antidotes ... administered as soon as possible once the patient/victim has been admitted to a medical care facility.'
methanol_poisoning.caveat: Both pages read through a fetch summary that quoted them; neither mentions Bali. Bali-specific risk comes only from the State Dept line in safety_health.drink_safety. No source here says how to tell a safe drink by look, taste or price - never claim one can.

water_safety.value: The State Department says that in many areas of Indonesia tap water is not safe to drink, that bottled water and beverages are generally safe if they are a major brand with an intact seal, that many restaurants and hotels serve tap water unless bottled water is requested, and that ice may be made from tap water. Water can be made safe by filtering, boiling, disinfecting or distilling. Impure water can cause typhoid, cholera, hepatitis and dysentery.
water_safety.support: State Dept Indonesia page, 'Water quality and food safety', read directly in Chrome: 'In many areas, tap water is not safe to drink. In some locations, tap water is not available every day. Bottled water and beverages are generally safe. Use major brands and ensure the seal is intact. Many restaurants and hotels serve tap water unless bottled water is specifically requested. You may want to request no ice in your drinks since it may be made using tap water. Make water safe by filtering, boiling, disinfecting, or distilling. Impure water can cause diseases like typhoid, cholera, hepatitis, and dysentery.'
water_safety.caveat: Says 'many areas' of Indonesia, not Bali by name. Nothing here says what any particular hotel, restaurant or ice supplier in Bali does.

food_water_cdc.value: CDC advice for destinations where tap water may be contaminated: do not drink tap water or use ice; drinks from unopened factory-sealed bottles or cans are safer; coffee or tea served steaming hot should be safe; brush teeth with bottled or disinfected water; skip fountain drinks; avoid raw foods and fresh salads; hot food should be served hot; avoid street food, or apply the same rules to it.
food_water_cdc.scope: travelers anywhere tap water may be contaminated
food_water_cdc.support: CDC 'Choose Safe Food and Drinks When Traveling' (via fetch, quoted): 'Do not drink the tap water in countries where the tap water might be contaminated.' 'Do not use ice in destinations with limited access to clean water'. 'Drinks from unopened, factory-sealed bottles or cans are safer than tap water.' 'Hot coffee or tea should be safe if it is served steaming hot.' 'Brush your teeth with bottled or disinfected water.' 'do not drink fountain drinks.' 'Avoid eating raw foods.' 'Avoid eating fresh salads'. 'Avoid eating food from street vendors. If you choose to eat street food, follow the same food safety rules.' 'Tap water can be disinfected by boiling, filtering, or chemically treating it.' The CDC Indonesia page (read in Chrome) links to this page under 'Eat and drink safely'.

bug_bites.value: The CDC says bugs such as mosquitoes can spread a number of diseases in Indonesia, many of which cannot be prevented with a vaccine or medicine. Its steps: cover exposed skin with long sleeves, long pants and hats; use insect repellent (DEET, picaridin, oil of lemon eucalyptus, IR3535 or 2-undecanone); use permethrin-treated clothing; stay in air-conditioned or screened rooms; use a bed net if the sleeping area is open to the outdoors.
bug_bites.support: CDC Indonesia page, 'Prevent bug bites', read directly in Chrome: 'Bugs (like mosquitoes, ticks, and fleas) can spread a number of diseases in Indonesia. Many of these diseases cannot be prevented with a vaccine or medicine.' 'Cover exposed skin by wearing long-sleeved shirts, long pants, and hats. Use an appropriate insect repellent. Use permethrin-treated clothing and gear ... Do not use permethrin directly on skin. Stay and sleep in air-conditioned or screened rooms. Use a bed net if the area where you are sleeping is exposed to the outdoors.' 'Use a repellent that contains 20% or more DEET for protection that lasts up to several hours.' Lists DEET, Picaridin, OLE/PMD, IR3535, 2-undecanone. Dengue row: transmission 'Mosquito bite', advice 'Avoid bug bites'. Page last reviewed August 25, 2026.

dengue.value: Dengue is spread mainly by the bite of an infected Aedes mosquito, and these mosquitoes bite during the day and night. The most common symptom is fever with aches and pains, eye pain, nausea, vomiting or rash, typically lasting 2 to 7 days. Warning signs of severe dengue, which is a medical emergency, usually begin in the 24 to 48 hours after the fever goes away: belly pain, repeated vomiting, bleeding from the nose or gums, blood in vomit or stool, extreme tiredness or restlessness. No dengue vaccine is currently available in the United States.
dengue.support: CDC dengue pages (via fetch, quoted): 'All four dengue viruses are spread to people primarily through the bite of an infected Aedes species mosquito.' 'Mosquitoes bite during the day and night.' 'The most common symptom of dengue is fever with any of the following: Aches and pains (eye pain, typically behind the eyes, muscle, joint, or bone pain)'; nausea, vomiting, rash. 'Symptoms of dengue typically last 2-7 days.' 'Warning signs usually begin in the 24-48 hours after fever has gone away.' 'Belly pain or tenderness; Vomiting (at least 3 times in 24 hours); Bleeding from the nose or gums; Vomiting blood, or blood in the stool; Feeling extremely tired or restless'. 'Severe dengue is a medical emergency'. 'There are no dengue vaccines currently available in the United States.' 'A blood test is the only way to confirm the diagnosis'. Returning travelers: 'prevent mosquito bites for 3 weeks'. CDC Indonesia page lists Dengue with 'Avoid bug bites'; an earlier reading of that page noted dengue risk throughout Indonesia.
dengue.caveat: No Bali case numbers or seasonality sourced; do not state a 'dengue season' or name pain relievers.

medical_care.value: The State Department says routine medical care is available in Indonesia's major cities, that adequate care may be harder to find in rural areas, that most foreigners with the resources leave the country for anything beyond basic procedures, and that medical staff may speak little or no English. Ambulance services are not widely available and can take 45 minutes or longer, so travelers may prefer a taxi or private vehicle to the hospital. The US embassy keeps a list of doctors and hospitals and does not endorse any.
medical_care.support: State Dept Indonesia page, read directly in Chrome: 'Health facilities are available throughout Indonesia. It may be harder to find adequate health care in rural areas. Routine medical care is available in major cities. Most foreigners in Indonesia who have the resources leave the country for anything beyond basic procedures.' 'Medical staff may speak little or no English. The U.S. embassy maintains a list of doctors and hospitals. The U.S. embassy does not endorse or recommend any specific medical provider or clinic.' 'Ambulance services are not widely available... Travelers may prefer to take a taxi or private vehicle to the hospital instead of waiting for an ambulance. Sometimes they can take 45 minutes or longer to arrive.' 'Dial 118 or 119 for emergency medical services.' 'If you get injured, you will likely need to travel to a major city for appropriate medical care.' 'Psychological and psychiatric services are limited'.
medical_care.caveat: Indonesia-wide; names no Bali hospital. Never name or rank a hospital or clinic.

medical_payment.value: Medical care is not free in Indonesia. The State Department says hospitals and doctors often require payment or sizable deposits upfront before service or admission, most care providers only accept cash, credit card payment is not always available, patients cover all costs of transfer between hospitals, most US health plans and Medicare do not cover care abroad, and the US government does not pay medical bills. It highly recommends travel insurance and strongly recommends supplemental insurance covering medical evacuation; with such insurance the traveler pays first and seeks reimbursement.
medical_payment.support: State Dept Indonesia page, read directly in Chrome: 'Make sure you know if your health insurance plan covers any medical expenses abroad. Most U.S. plans do not. The U.S. government does not pay medical bills. U.S. Medicare and Medicaid do not cover expenses or bills abroad. Most hospitals and doctors abroad do not accept U.S. health insurance. Medical care is not free in Indonesia. If you require medical attention, you will incur expenses, even if you are treated in a public healthcare facility. Most care providers overseas only accept cash payments. Credit card payment is not always available.' 'The U.S. government strongly recommends supplemental insurance to cover medical evacuation. If you purchase supplemental insurance, you are responsible for seeking reimbursement from the insurance provider.' 'Hospitals and doctors often require payment or sizable deposits upfront prior to service or admission. Patients must cover all costs for transfer to or between hospitals.' 'We highly recommend that you buy travel insurance before you travel. Check with your travel insurance provider about evacuation assistance, medical insurance, and trip cancelation coverage.'
medical_payment.caveat: No amounts. Never print a deposit, bill or premium figure, and never say what an insurer will or will not pay.

medication_letter.value: The State Department says to carry prescription medication in its original packaging with the prescription and a doctor's letter giving the patient name as in the passport, the medication name and daily dose, and confirmation it is for personal use; to declare all prescription medication on the All Indonesia arrival card; to hand-carry it; and never to mail or ship medication to Indonesia, where recipients of mailed medicines may be detained or arrested.
medication_letter.support: State Dept, read directly in Chrome: 'Always carry your prescription medication in original packaging, along with your doctor's prescription. If you enter Indonesia with prescription medication, bring a letter from your doctor with the following details: Patient name, which should match the passport; Medication name and daily dosage amount; Confirmation the medication is for personal use only. All prescription medication must be declared on the All Indonesia website.' 'You should only hand-carry prescription medications into the country. Do not mail or ship medications to Indonesia. Authorities closely monitor packages containing pharmaceuticals. They may detain or arrest recipients of any prescription or over-the-counter medications.' 'Marijuana, cannabis, hash, edibles, and products containing CBD or THC are illegal in Indonesia. A medical prescription does not make these substances legal.'

crime.value: The State Department says US citizens have been victims of violent crimes in Indonesia, especially in Bali, and that pickpocketing, sexual assault, vehicle theft, snatch-and-grab robberies and residential break-ins are common. Its advice: avoid isolated areas late at night, watch bags and luggage, carry only essential items, safeguard passport and bank cards, avoid traveling alone, and be mindful of phones near roadways where snatch-and-grab crimes occur.
crime.support: State Dept, read directly in Chrome 2026-10-13: 'U.S. citizens have been victims of violent crimes in Indonesia, especially in Bali. Pickpocketing, sexual assault, vehicle theft, snatch-and-grab robberies, and residential break-ins are common. Avoid isolated areas late at night. Stay aware of your surroundings, especially vehicles or individuals that might be following you... Monitor bags and luggage. Carry only essential items, safeguard your passport and bank cards, and avoid traveling alone.' 'Always carry a cell phone, but be mindful of your surroundings, such as crowded places or near roadways where snatch and grab crimes may occur.'

scams.value: The State Department says internet romance and financial scams happen in Indonesia, warns travelers to be careful of anyone asking for money, including people who claim local authorities want money, and notes that counterfeit and pirated goods are common and may have to be surrendered or may bring fines on return to the United States.
scams.support: State Dept, read directly: 'Internet romance and financial scams happen in Indonesia. Be careful of anyone asking for money, especially those who start a "romantic" relationship online or claim local authorities want money.' 'Counterfeit and pirated goods are common in many destinations... You may be subject to fines or have to surrender counterfeit and pirated goods to authorities if you bring them back to the United States.'
scams.caveat: The page lists no Bali street scams (money-changer sleight of hand, taxi meters, etc.). Those are NOT sourced; describe none of them as fact.

counterfeit_medication.value: The State Department says pharmaceuticals in Indonesia are usually easy to buy with few controls, that counterfeit medication is common and may not work, may have the wrong strength or may contain dangerous ingredients, and that travelers should buy medication with the help of a medical professional and from trusted places.
counterfeit_medication.support: State Dept, read directly: 'Exercise caution when purchasing medication abroad. Pharmaceuticals are usually easy to buy with few controls. Counterfeit medication is common and may not work, have the wrong strength, or have dangerous ingredients. You should buy medication with the help of a medical professional and from trusted places.'

travelers_diarrhea.value: The CDC calls travelers' diarrhea the most common travel-related illness and lists Asia, except Japan and South Korea, among the highest-risk destinations. In otherwise healthy adults it is rarely serious or life-threatening. Prevention: eat only food that is cooked and served hot, avoid buffets, drink only from factory-sealed containers, avoid ice, and wash hands often with soap and water. Treatment: drink lots of fluids, use oral rehydration solution in serious cases; over-the-counter drugs such as loperamide treat the symptoms; antibiotics from a doctor should be considered only for severe cases.
travelers_diarrhea.support: CDC (via fetch, quoted): 'Travelers' diarrhea is the most common travel-related illness.' 'The highest-risk destinations are in Asia (except for Japan and South Korea) as well as the Middle East, Africa, Mexico, and Central and South America.' 'In otherwise healthy adults, diarrhea is rarely serious or life-threatening, but it can make a trip very unpleasant.' 'Eat only foods that are cooked and served hot. Avoid food that has been sitting on a buffet.' 'Only drink beverages from factory-sealed containers, and avoid ice because it may have been made from unclean water.' 'Wash your hands often with soap and water, especially after using the bathroom and before eating.' 'If you get diarrhea, drink lots of fluids to stay hydrated. In serious cases of travelers' diarrhea, oral rehydration solution...can be used for fluid replacements.' 'Several drugs, such as loperamide, can be bought over-the-counter to treat the symptoms of diarrhea.' 'Your doctor may give you antibiotics to treat travelers' diarrhea, but consider using them only for severe cases.'
travelers_diarrhea.caveat: Not Bali-specific; gives no duration and no percentages. Do not state how long it lasts or how many travelers get it.

jet_lag.value: The CDC says jet lag is caused by a mismatch between a person's normal daily rhythms and a new time zone and can affect mood, concentration and physical and mental performance. Its advice: shift bedtime an hour or two toward the destination for a few days before travel (later going west, earlier going east); on the flight eat small meals, avoid alcohol, drink plenty of water and use caffeine strategically but not in the evening; after arrival stay in well-lit areas during the day, follow the destination's schedule, keep naps to 15 to 20 minutes, and arrive at least 2 days before any important event.
jet_lag.support: CDC jet lag page (via fetch, quoted): 'Jet lag is caused by a mismatch between a person's normal daily rhythms and a new time zone.' 'Jet lag can affect your mood, your ability to concentrate, and your physical and mental performance.' Westbound 'go to bed an hour or two later than usual'; eastbound 'an hour or two earlier'. 'at least 2 days before any important events, to give your body time to adjust'. 'Eat small meals to avoid stomach aches'; 'Avoid alcohol as it disrupts sleep'; 'Use caffeine and exercise strategically...avoid these in the evening'; 'Drink plenty of water'; naps 'no more than 15-20 minutes'; 'Stay in well-lit areas at your destination during the day.' 'Take any medicine or sleep aids as directed by your healthcare provider.'
jet_lag.caveat: No statement on melatonin or on days-per-time-zone recovery. Do not state either.

diving.value: The State Department says diving in Indonesia can be dangerous because of minimal safety regulations.
diving.support: State Dept Indonesia page, 'Adventure travel - Water sports', read directly in Chrome 2026-10-13: 'Diving can be dangerous due to minimal safety regulations.'
diving.caveat: One sentence only was captured; the surrounding advice was not read. Say nothing more specific than this.

sun_and_outdoors.value: The CDC's outdoor advice for Indonesia: use sunscreen with an SPF of at least 15, wear protective clothing, seek shade during the hottest time of day (10 a.m. to 4 p.m.), remember that sunlight reflects off sand and water, eat and drink regularly in the heat, and avoid swimming or wading in water that may be contaminated after flooding. It also advises keeping away from animals.
sun_and_outdoors.support: CDC Indonesia page, 'Stay safe outdoors', read directly in Chrome: 'Protect yourself from UV radiation: use sunscreen with an SPF of at least 15, wear protective clothing, and seek shade during the hottest time of day (10 a.m.-4 p.m.)... Because sunlight reflects off snow, sand, and water, sun exposure may be increased during activities like skiing, swimming, and sailing.' 'Heat-related illness, such as heat stroke, can be deadly. Eat and drink regularly, wear loose and lightweight clothing'. Section heading 'Keep away from animals'. Flood notice: 'avoid swimming or wading in water that may be contaminated'.

driving_permit.value: A US driver's license alone is not recognized in Indonesia; foreign drivers must carry an International Driving Permit. AAA, which issues the permit in the US, lists Indonesia as honoring it. Motorcycle helmets are required.
driving_permit.scope: US license holders driving or riding in Indonesia
driving_permit.support: State Dept: 'A valid U.S. driver's license alone is not recognized for driving in Indonesia. Foreign drivers must carry an International Driving Permit.' 'Motorcycle helmets are required.' AAA country list: 'Indonesia*' - 'Not party to 1949 Convention: International Driving Permit Honored.'
driving_permit.caveat: Does NOT by itself establish which licence class a scooter needs - see getting_around.licence_must_match_vehicle for the statute.
driving_permit.writing_rule: Scooter articles: a permit is required and the AAA permit is honored (this record). The law requires a licence matching the vehicle type and has a separate motorcycle class (licence_must_match_vehicle). So tell readers plainly that a US licence without a motorcycle endorsement does not match a scooter under Indonesian law, and that insurers look at the same thing. Never write that a car licence plus permit 'works'.

accident_and_police.value: After a traffic accident, stay at the scene and notify police. Carry ID and the vehicle registration. In car-motorcycle collisions the driver of the larger vehicle is often presumed responsible. If fined, ask for an official receipt; travelers occasionally report requests for unofficial payments.
accident_and_police.scope: visitors driving or riding in Indonesia
accident_and_police.support: State Dept: 'Drivers involved in traffic accidents should remain at the scene and notify police.' 'In collisions involving cars and motorcycles, the driver of the larger vehicle is often presumed responsible.' 'If you are issued a fine, request an official receipt.'

ride_hailing.value: Grab and Gojek operate in Indonesia, and licensed taxis are widely available in major cities; the State Department describes Blue Bird taxis as generally the most reliable.
ride_hailing.scope: Indonesia generally; Bali-specific pickup restrictions are NOT covered
ride_hailing.support: State Dept: 'Licensed taxis and ride-hailing services are widely available in major Indonesian cities. Blue bird taxis are generally considered the most reliable and professional... Grab and Gojek are also av[ailable]'.

circular_driving_rules.value: Bali's 2025 circular requires foreign tourists who drive or ride to hold a valid international or national driving licence, obey traffic rules, wear a helmet, not carry more passengers than the vehicle allows, and not be under the influence of alcohol or drugs. It also requires them to use roadworthy four-wheeled transport that officially belongs to a rental business or association.
circular_driving_rules.support: Read directly: 'memiliki Surat Izin Mengemudi Internasional atau Nasional yang masih berlaku, tertib berlalu lintas di jalan, berpakaian sopan, menggunakan helm, mengikuti rambu-rambu lalu lintas, tidak memuat penumpang melebihi kapasitas, serta tidak dalam pengaruh minuman beralkohol dan/atau obat-obatan terlarang. Wisman juga diwajibkan menggunakan alat transportasi laik pakai roda 4 yang resmi bernaung di bawah badan usaha atau asosiasi penyewaan transportasi roda 4.'
circular_driving_rules.writing_rule: This is the province's own statement of the licence rule. It still does not say which licence CLASS a scooter needs. The four-wheel wording concerns rented cars; do not stretch it into a claim that scooter rental is banned.

grab_at_airport.value: Grab operates airport pickups at Bali's airport from a GrabCar Lounge at the International Arrival Terminal; rides are booked in the app, with car, premium car, electric car, motorbike and advance-booking options.
grab_at_airport.scope: arriving passengers at I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport, international terminal
grab_at_airport.support: Grab's own airport page: pickup point 'GrabCar Lounge International Arrival Terminal Ngurah Rai International Airport'; services listed include GrabCar Airport, GrabBike, GrabCar Premium Airport, GrabCar Electric Airport and Advance Booking.
grab_at_airport.caveat: Read through a summarising fetch of the operator's page, not line by line. The page gives no fees, hours or domestic-terminal pickup point, and says nothing about Gojek. Corrects the secondary claim seen earlier that ride apps cannot pick up at the terminal.

licence_must_match_vehicle.value: Indonesia's traffic law requires every driver to hold a licence matching the type of vehicle driven, and it has a separate licence class for motorcycles (SIM C) distinct from the car class (SIM A). A foreign licence is valid in Indonesia where a bilateral or multilateral agreement provides for it.
licence_must_match_vehicle.scope: anyone driving or riding a motor vehicle on Indonesian roads
licence_must_match_vehicle.support: Law 22 of 2009, full text on the Finance Ministry's legal database, read directly. Pasal 77(1): 'Setiap orang yang mengemudikan Kendaraan Bermotor di Jalan wajib memiliki Surat Izin Mengemudi sesuai dengan jenis Kendaraan Bermotor yang dikemudikan.' Pasal 80: 'Surat Izin Mengemudi A berlaku untuk mengemudikan mobil penumpang dan barang perseorangan...; Surat Izin Mengemudi C berlaku untuk mengemudikan Sepeda Motor'. Pasal 85(4): 'Surat Izin Mengemudi yang diterbitkan oleh negara lain berlaku di Indonesia' where a bilateral or multilateral agreement exists.
licence_must_match_vehicle.writing_rule: This is the legal footing for the scooter articles: the law ties the licence to the vehicle type and treats motorcycles as their own class. It follows that a car-only entitlement does not match a scooter. State that reasoning as the law's logic; the statute does not mention international permits by category, so do not claim it does.
licence_must_match_vehicle.caveat: The 2009 text as published; later amendments were not checked.

traffic_penalties.value: Under Indonesia's traffic law, driving without the required licence carries up to 4 months' detention or a fine of up to IDR 1,000,000. Being unable to show a valid licence carries up to 1 month and/or up to IDR 250,000. Riding a motorcycle without a national-standard helmet, or letting a passenger ride without one, carries up to 1 month or up to IDR 250,000.
traffic_penalties.scope: anyone driving or riding a motor vehicle on Indonesian roads
traffic_penalties.support: Law 22 of 2009, read directly. Pasal 281: 'tidak memiliki Surat Izin Mengemudi ... pidana kurungan paling lama 4 (empat) bulan atau denda paling banyak Rp1.000.000,00'. Pasal 288(2): 'tidak dapat menunjukkan Surat Izin Mengemudi yang sah ... kurungan paling lama 1 (satu) bulan dan/atau denda paling banyak Rp250.000,00'. Pasal 291(1)-(2): helmet, 'kurungan paling lama 1 (satu) bulan atau denda paling banyak Rp250.000,00'.
traffic_penalties.display_rule: rupiah maxima from the statute; never convert to a frozen dollar figure
traffic_penalties.caveat: Statutory maximums from the 2009 text; amounts actually charged at a roadside stop are a different matter and are not sourced.

taxi_safety.value: The State Department says licensed taxis and ride-hailing services are widely available in major Indonesian cities, that Blue Bird taxis are generally considered the most reliable, and that Grab and Gojek show driver identification, vehicle information and the fare in the app. Its advice: arrange transport through reputable taxi companies or ride-hailing apps, confirm driver and vehicle before getting in, avoid unlicensed taxis that solicit passengers directly, particularly at airports and tourist areas, check for a working meter, and share trip details through the app.
taxi_safety.support: State Dept, read directly: 'Licensed taxis and ride-hailing services are widely available in major Indonesian cities. Blue bird taxis are generally considered the most reliable and professional ride-hail service. Grab and Gojek are also available options. They provide driver identification, vehicle information, and fare transparency through mobile applications. Arrange transportation through reputable taxi companies or ride-hailing applications. Confirm driver and vehicle information before entering the vehicle. Avoid unlicensed taxis that solicit passengers directly, particularly in airports, tourist areas, and transportation hubs. Most taxi and ride-hail trips occur without issues.' 'Before fully entering the taxi, match the photo on the dashboard ID with the driver. Make sure there is a working meter.'
