road_distances.writing_rule: Give distances in miles for Americans (km x 0.62), rounded, with 'about'. Drive TIMES stay serve-live: tell readers to check a live map at the hour they will travel. The point to make is that short distances take long.

qr_payments_us.value: Indonesia's cross-border QR payment scheme connects Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Japan, South Korea and China. The United States is not connected, so a US bank app or wallet cannot pay a QRIS code through it.
qr_payments_us.scope: US visitors paying merchants in Indonesia
qr_payments_us.support: Bank Indonesia, read directly in a browser: 'Saat ini, QRIS Antarnegara telah digunakan untuk transaksi QRIS di Thailand, Malaysia, Singapura, Jepang, Korea Selatan Dan Tiongkok baik oleh wisatawan Indonesia maupun turis asing.' The page's provider table lists only those six countries; neither 'Amerika' nor 'United States' appears anywhere in the page text. Foreign users pay by opening their own payment app, scanning, entering the rupiah amount and confirming in their own currency.
qr_payments_us.caveat: Says nothing about third-party tourist wallets.

changers_and_rupiah.value: Bali's 2025 circular tells foreign tourists to change money only at authorised money changers, bank or non-bank, identified by a licence number and a Bank Indonesia QR-code logo, to pay with the Indonesian standard QR code, and to transact in rupiah.
changers_and_rupiah.support: Read directly: 'penukaran mata uang asing di penyelenggara Kegiatan Usaha Penukaran Valuta Asing (KUPVA) resmi (authorized money changer), baik Bank maupun non-Bank yang ditandai dengan adanya nomor izin dan logo QR code dari Bank Indonesia, melakukan pembayaran dengan menggunakan Kode QR Standar Indonesia dan melakukan transaksi dengan menggunakan mata uang [rupiah]'.
changers_and_rupiah.writing_rule: Pair with money.qr_payments_us: the province tells visitors to pay by QR, while the central bank's cross-border scheme does not include the US. Say both.

bill_tax_badung.value: In Badung regency, the local tax on restaurant food and drink and on hotel stays is 10%. Entertainment at discos, karaoke venues, nightclubs, bars and steam baths/spas is taxed at 40%.
bill_tax_badung.scope: Badung regency, Bali (Kuta, Legian, Seminyak, Canggu, Jimbaran, Uluwatu and Nusa Dua); other regencies set their own rates
bill_tax_badung.support: Badung revenue agency Circular 973/14315/Bapenda dated 29 December 2023, scanned PDF read page by page: 'Pajak Barang dan Jasa Tertentu: Makanan dan/atau minuman 10% ... Jasa Perhotelan 10% ... Jasa Kesenian dan Hiburan 10% - Khusus jasa hiburan pada diskotek, karaoke, kelab malam, bar, dan mandi uap/spa sebesar 40%'. Regional Regulation 7/2023, in force from 1 January 2024.
bill_tax_badung.caveat: A 2023 circular: the 40% entertainment rate was publicly contested after it took effect, so re-check for amendments before stating it as current. Says nothing about 'service charge', which is a business practice, not a tax; Ubud is in Gianyar regency and is not covered.

bill_tax_gianyar.value: In Gianyar regency, which includes Ubud, the local tax on restaurant food and drink and on hotel stays is 10%. Discos, karaoke venues, nightclubs, bars and steam baths/spas are taxed at 40%; traditional folk arts and entertainment at 5%.
bill_tax_gianyar.support: Gianyar Regional Regulation 7 of 2023 on regional taxes, text as mirrored on pasal.id, read directly. Pasal 27: '(1) Tarif PBJT ditetapkan sebesar 10% (sepuluh persen). (2) Khusus tarif PBJT atas kesenian dan hiburan rakyat/tradisional ditetapkan 5% (lima persen) (3) Khusus tarif PBJT atas jasa hiburan pada diskotek, karaoke, kelab malam, bar, dan mandi uap/spa ditetapkan 40% (empat puluh persen).' The regency's own legal database lists the regulation (enacted 5 December 2023) but serves it as a PDF that was not opened.
bill_tax_gianyar.caveat: Secondary because the text was read on a legal-text mirror, not the regency's own copy. Same rates as Badung. Amendments since 2023 not checked; says nothing about service charges.

service_charge.value: In Indonesia a service charge is an amount added on top of the listed price for service at hotels and hotel restaurants. Under a Manpower Ministry regulation it must be distributed to the workers, half shared equally and the rest by seniority and performance, after allowances for breakage or loss and for staff development.
service_charge.scope: hotels and restaurants in hotels in Indonesia; the regulation does not cover standalone restaurants
service_charge.support: Manpower Ministry legal-information page (29 October 2018) on Ministerial Regulation 7 of 2016, read directly: 'uang servis adalah tambahan dari tariff yang sudah ditetapkan sebelumnya dalam rangka jasa pelayanan pada usaha hotel dan usaha restoran di hotel'; 'Uang servis wajib dibagikan kepada pekerja/buruh ... 50% (lima puluh persen) dibagi sama besar dan sisanya dibagi berdasarkan senioritas dan kinerja'; used for 'Penggantian atas terjadinya resiko kehilangan atau kerusakan; Pendayagunaan peningkatan kualitas sumber daya manusia; dan Dibagikan kepada pekerja/buruh'.
service_charge.caveat: Sets no percentage. The rate a hotel adds is its own choice and is not sourced; never print a service-charge percentage.
service_charge.writing_rule: Distinguish clearly: the 10% is a local TAX (sourced per regency); the service charge is a separate business charge that goes to staff by regulation.

card_fraud.value: The State Department says credit card fraud is common in Indonesia and that criminals skim bank cards to reach victims' accounts. Its advice: use ATMs in secure locations such as major bank branches, check machines for tampering, and monitor account statements regularly.
card_fraud.support: State Dept, read directly: 'Credit card fraud is common in Indonesia. Criminals "skim" bank cards to access victims' bank accounts. Use ATMs in secure locations, such as major bank branches, and check machines for tampering. Regularly monitor your account statements.'

atm_us_cards.value: The State Department says Indonesia has ATMs that accept US-issued bank cards, which may charge a currency conversion or transaction fee; that most establishments accept credit cards; that travelers should check with their card issuer or bank for international transaction fees; and that carrying some cash in smaller denominations may be helpful.
atm_us_cards.support: State Dept 'Currency', read directly: 'The Indonesian rupiah is the official currency of Indonesia. Most establishments accept credit cards. Please check with your credit card or banking institution for any international transaction fees. Carrying some cash, especially in smaller denominations, may be helpful. Indonesia has ATMs that accept U.S.-issued bankcards. But they may charge a currency conversion or a transaction fee. You can also get cash through Western Union in Indonesia for a fee.'
atm_us_cards.caveat: No amounts: withdrawal limits and fee figures remain unsourced. Never print one.

phone_registration.value: A short-stay visitor does not need to register a foreign phone's IMEI if the phone stays on its home SIM using roaming, or if the visitor uses an Indonesian SIM registered at a mobile operator's outlet, which gives network access for up to 90 days.
phone_registration.scope: foreign tourists and short business visitors
phone_registration.support: Customs IMEI FAQ: 'Jika hanya tinggal sementara (ex: turis, keperluan bisnis)... Pendaftaran IMEI tidak diperlukan, jika HKT asal luar negeri yang digunakan di Indonesia: tetap menggunakan SIM card dari negara asal (roaming), atau; Perangkat HKT wisatawan asing menggunakan SIM card Indonesia dengan melakukan registrasi di gerai operator seluler untuk mendapat akses jaringan telekomunikasi paling lama 90 hari.' (Permen Kominfo 1/2020)

tourist_circular.value: Bali's current rulebook for visitors is Governor's Circular No. 7 of 2025, 'New Order for Foreign Tourists While in Bali'. It replaced the 2023 list. Violations are to be dealt with firmly under Indonesian law, and residents are asked to report them to a provincial WhatsApp hotline.
tourist_circular.support: Bali provincial media centre, read directly: 'Gubernur Bali Wayan Koster mengeluarkan Surat Edaran Nomor 7 Tahun 2025 Tentang Tatanan Baru bagi Wisatawan Asing selama Berada di Bali' (Senin, 24 Maret 2025). The 2023 circular (No. 4 of 2023) is referenced in provincial documents as the earlier version.
tourist_circular.caveat: Source is the province's own news release about the circular, not the circular's PDF. 'Replaced the 2023 list' is my reading of the sequence, not a quoted line.

temple_access.value: Foreign tourists may not enter the inner and middle courtyards of a temple or other sanctified place unless they are there to pray, in Balinese traditional dress; the circular adds that they must not be menstruating. Climbing sacred trees, climbing on sacred structures, and posing indecently or unclothed at sacred sites are prohibited.
temple_access.support: Read directly: 'larangan bagi turis asing untuk memasuki Utamaning Mandala dan Madyaning Mandala tempat suci atau tempat yang disucikan seperti Pura, Pelinggih, kecuali untuk keperluan bersembahyang dengan memakai busana Adat Bali atau persembahyangan, dan tidak sedang datang bulan (menstruasi). Wisatawan asing dilarang memanjat pohon yang disakralkan'.
temple_access.writing_rule: Report the menstruation rule as what the circular says, neutrally, without endorsing or mocking it.

conduct_and_plastics.value: The circular requires modest dress and polite conduct in sacred areas, tourist sites, restaurants, shops and on the road, and prohibits littering, single-use plastics (plastic bags, styrofoam, plastic straws, plastic-packaged drinks), abusive or aggressive behavior toward officials, locals or other tourists, spreading hate speech or hoaxes online, and working or doing business without official papers.
conduct_and_plastics.support: Read directly: 'dilarang menggunakan plastik sekali pakai seperti kantong plastik, polysterina (styrofoam), sedotan plastik, dan minuman kemasan plastik. ... dilarang mengucapkan kata-kata kasar, berperilaku tidak sopan, membuat keributan, serta bertindak agresif'.

galungan_meaning.value: Galungan marks the victory of dharma (good) over adharma (evil) and falls every 210 days in the Balinese Pawukon calendar; Kuningan follows ten days later and closes the festival. Families pray at home and at temples, ancestral spirits are believed to visit during the period, and penjor, curved bamboo poles decorated with produce, stand as a sign of gratitude. The day before Galungan is Penampahan.
galungan_meaning.support: Article on the Finance Ministry's Bali-Nusa Tenggara regional office site, dated 18 June 2026 (via fetch, quoted): 'Galungan menjadi simbol kemenangan Dharma (kebenaran, kebajikan, dan kesucian) atas Adharma'; 'setiap 210 hari sekali berdasarkan kalender Pawukon, tepatnya pada hari Budha Kliwon Wuku Dungulan'; 'Penjor, yang terbuat dari bambu melengkung dan dihias dengan hasil bumi, melambangkan rasa syukur'; Penampahan the day before; Kuningan ten days later; family prayers at homes and temples; ancestral spirits visit.
galungan_meaning.caveat: A government office's explanatory article, not a religious authority. Says nothing about closures, traffic or prices; make no claims about those.

licensed_accommodation.value: Bali's 2025 circular requires foreign tourists to stay in accommodation businesses that hold a licence under the regulations.
licensed_accommodation.support: Read directly: 'wisatawan asing wajib tinggal/menginap di tempat usaha akomodasi yang memiliki izin sesuai ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan'.

nyepi_2027.value: Nyepi in 2027 is Monday, March 8 (Saka New Year 1949), a national holiday. Eid al-Fitr follows on Wednesday and Thursday, March 10-11, with collective leave days on March 9, 12 and 15.
nyepi_2027.scope: Indonesia; the day of silence itself is observed in Bali
nyepi_2027.support: State Secretariat, read directly: 'Senin, 8 Maret 2027: Hari Suci Nyepi (Tahun Baru Saka 1949); Rabu-Kamis, 10-11 Maret 2027: Idulfitri 1448 Hijriah', from Joint Decree 'Nomor 1205 Tahun 2026, Nomor 3 Tahun 2026, dan Nomor 2 Tahun 2026 tentang Hari Libur Nasional dan Cuti Bersama Tahun 2027'.
nyepi_2027.writing_rule: Articles are evergreen: give the 2027 date as an example and tell readers the date moves each year. Airport closure hours are NOT in this record.

galungan_kuningan_2027.value: In 2027 Galungan falls on Wednesday, January 13, and again on August 11; Kuningan follows ten days later, on Saturday, January 23, and on August 21. The pair recurs every 210 days.
galungan_kuningan_2027.support: The Religious Affairs Ministry's 2027 Hindu holiday letter could not be opened (its server refused connections from the terminal and from Chrome). Google's index of that PDF shows: 'Hari Penampahan Galungan (Libur Fakultatif). 3 Rabu, 13 Januari 2027 ... Hari Penampahan Kuningan (Libur Fakultatif). 6 Sabtu, 23 Januari'. The August dates (11 and 21 August 2027) come from the Kalender Bali listing and a Bali site in the same results; all sources agree.
galungan_kuningan_2027.caveat: Marked secondary because the letter itself was not opened - only Google's snippet of it. Re-open the PDF when the ministry server is back. An earlier snippet that seemed to show 14 January was the following day's entry (Umanis Galungan), not a conflict.
galungan_kuningan_2027.writing_rule: Evergreen articles: give 2027 as the worked example and explain the 210-day cycle.

nyepi_data_shutdown.value: On Nyepi, mobile data and television and radio broadcasts in Bali are switched off for 24 hours, from 6 a.m. on the day to 6 a.m. the next morning. In 2026 that ran from 06:00 on Thursday, March 19, to 06:00 on Friday, March 20. Hospitals and other vital services are exempt, and operators warn customers by text message in the days before.
nyepi_data_shutdown.scope: Bali province on Nyepi; hours stated for 2026
nyepi_data_shutdown.support: Circular No. 2 of 2026 of the Minister of Communication and Digital Affairs, signed 12 March 2026, scanned PDF on the Bali provincial government's site, read page by page: operators are asked to 'menonaktifkan dan/atau menghentikan layanan internet melalui jaringan seluler serta distribusi dan/atau transmisi konten siaran televisi dan radio pada hari Kamis tanggal 19 Maret 2026 pukul 06.00 WITA sampai dengan hari Jumat tanggal 20 Maret 2026 pukul 06.00 WITA', keeping service at vital objects listed in Annex I (28 hospitals and more); SMS notices on 12, 16, 17 and 18 March.
nyepi_data_shutdown.caveat: The circular is an appeal to operators (himbauan) and covers mobile data and broadcasts, not fixed-line internet; a news report says hotel Wi-Fi stayed on. Confirms Nyepi 2026 was 19 March and that the observance window runs 6 a.m. to 6 a.m.
nyepi_data_shutdown.writing_rule: Give 2026 as the worked example; 2027 hours are not announced.

national_holidays_2027.value: Indonesia's 2027 national holidays include New Year (January 1), Chinese New Year (February 6), Nyepi (March 8), Eid al-Fitr (March 10-11), Good Friday (March 26), Labor Day (May 1), Ascension Day (May 6), Eid al-Adha (May 17), Vesak (May 20), Pancasila Day (June 1), Islamic New Year (June 6), Independence Day (August 17) and Christmas (December 25), with collective leave days on February 5, March 9, 12 and 15, March 25, May 18 and 19, and December 24.
national_holidays_2027.support: State Secretariat page on the three-minister Joint Decree No. 1205/2026, 3/2026 and 2/2026, signed 15 September 2026 (read directly earlier for Nyepi; full list re-read via fetch): 1 Jan New Year; 5 Jan Isra Mikraj; 6 Feb Chinese New Year; 8 Mar Nyepi; 10-11 Mar Idulfitri; 26 Mar Good Friday; 28 Mar Easter; 1 May Labour Day; 6 May Ascension; 17 May Iduladha; 20 May Vesak; 1 Jun Pancasila Day; 6 Jun Islamic New Year; 15 Aug Prophet's Birthday; 17 Aug Independence Day; 25 Dec Christmas. Collective leave: 5 Feb; 9, 12, 15 Mar; 25 Mar; 18 May; 19 May; 24 Dec.
national_holidays_2027.caveat: Islamic holiday dates are set in advance and can shift by a day. The decree fixes public holidays; it does not say what any shop, attraction or office in Bali does on them. Galungan and Kuningan are not national holidays.
national_holidays_2027.writing_rule: 2027 is the worked example; tell readers the list is issued each year.

climate_normals.value: Monthly climate normals for Denpasar/Ngurah Rai (south Bali): rainfall is about 351 mm in January, 290 in February, 231 in March, 107 in April, 95 in May, 68 in June, 28 in July, 36 in August, 59 in September, 64 in October, 131 in November and 327 in December. Mean temperature stays between 26.3 C (August) and 28.2 C (November) all year.
climate_normals.scope: south Bali (Denpasar/Ngurah Rai station, 8.75 S 115.17 E)
climate_normals.support: Japan Meteorological Agency, Tokyo Climate Center, 'Normals Data: DENPASAR/NGURAH RAI - INDONESIA', table read directly in Chrome: month, temperature C, precipitation mm: 1 27.9 350.7; 2 28.0 289.8; 3 28.0 231.1; 4 28.1 107.4; 5 27.8 94.7; 6 27.2 67.9; 7 26.5 27.6; 8 26.3 36.4; 9 26.8 59.4; 10 27.6 64.4; 11 28.2 131.2; 12 28.0 327.4.
climate_normals.caveat: The page does not state the averaging period. One station at sea level in the south: Ubud, the central mountains and the north differ and are NOT covered. Normals are long-run averages, not a forecast; say nothing about rain days or hours of rain per day.
climate_normals.writing_rule: Convert for Americans: 25.4 mm = 1 inch; 26.3-28.2 C = about 79-83 F. Describe months as wetter/drier by these numbers; never promise weather.

dry_season_bmkg.value: Indonesia's meteorological agency BMKG forecasts the dry season zone by zone each year. For 2026 it predicted an earlier-than-normal start across most of Java, Bali and Nusa Tenggara, with zones entering the dry season from April through June and the peak in August.
dry_season_bmkg.support: BMKG press release, 4 March 2026 (via fetch, quoted): 'sebagian besar wilayah Indonesia akan memasuki musim kemarau tahun 2026 lebih awal'; early onset in 'sebagian besar Sumatra, Jawa, Bali, Nusa Tenggara, Kalimantan bagian selatan dan timur'; 114 zones from April, 184 in May, 163 in June; 'puncak musim kemarau di sebagian besar wilayah Indonesia diprediksi terjadi pada bulan Agustus 2026'; drier than normal in 64.5% of zones.
dry_season_bmkg.caveat: A forecast for one year. Shows that season start dates move year to year; use it for that point only.

surf_by_coast.value: Bali surf guides agree on a seasonal split: in the dry season, roughly April to October, southeast trade winds blow offshore on the west-facing coast (Uluwatu, Padang Padang, Kuta, Canggu) and the largest swells arrive from June to August; in the wet season, roughly November to March, winds turn northwest and the east-facing coast (Keramas, Sanur, Nusa Dua) has the cleaner conditions.
surf_by_coast.support: Search-result summaries of several Bali surf-camp and surf-guide pages (Rapture Camps month-by-month guide, Bali Surfing Camp conditions FAQ, Indonesian Surf Guide): 'dry season (April to October) and the wet season (November to March)'; 'southeast trade winds dominate, creating ideal conditions for many of Bali's west coast breaks... Uluwatu, Padang Padang, and Impossibles'; 'June, July and August, when the most powerful swells of the year arrive'; wet season 'northwest winds... excellent opportunities at east coast locations like Keramas and Nusa Dua'.
surf_by_coast.caveat: Commercial surf operators, read as search summaries, not an official body. No wave heights, no claims about a named break's difficulty or safety. Attribute to 'surf guides'.

no_us_nonstop.value: There is no nonstop flight between the United States and Bali. The longest nonstop route from Bali's airport is to Istanbul, about 13 hours, and US cities are listed only as destinations that require a stopover.
no_us_nonstop.scope: scheduled passenger flights at Bali's airport (DPS) as listed in October 2026
no_us_nonstop.support: FlightConnections, page dated 2 October 2026, read directly: 'Denpasar Airport has non-stop passenger flights scheduled to 65 destinations in 19 countries.' 'The longest flight from Denpasar DPS is a 6,429 mile (10,346 km) non-stop route to Istanbul IST. This direct flight takes around 13 hours and is operated by Turkish Airlines.' Under 'popular destinations from Denpasar that require a stopover': Chicago, Dallas-Fort Worth, Atlanta, Denver, Newark.
no_us_nonstop.caveat: A schedule-data aggregator, not an airline or the airport. Schedules change; re-check before each batch that states it. Gives no door-to-door times from US airports - those stay serve-live.

dps_hub_routes.value: Schedule data for Bali's airport (October 2026) lists nonstop flights from hubs including Singapore, Kuala Lumpur, Bangkok, Manila, Hong Kong, Taipei, Seoul, Tokyo, Sydney, Dubai, Doha and Istanbul, and no US city. Listed nonstop times to Bali run from about 3.5 hours (Singapore) through about 5 to 6 hours (Hong Kong, Taipei), about 7 to 8 hours (Seoul, Tokyo), about 10 hours (Dubai, Doha) and about 13 hours (Istanbul).
dps_hub_routes.support: Aerocorner DPS page, data dated 9 October 2026 (via fetch): 41 international routes, 46 airlines; Singapore 3 hr 25 (Singapore Airlines, Scoot, Garuda and others); Kuala Lumpur 3 hr 45; Tokyo NRT 7 hr 40 (Garuda); Seoul ICN 7 hr 20 (Korean Air, Jeju Air); Taipei 5 hr 40 (China Airlines, EVA Air, Starlux); Hong Kong 5 hr 20 (Cathay Pacific, Hong Kong Airlines); Manila 4 hr 20; Bangkok 4 hr 55; Doha 10 hr 30 (Qatar Airways); Dubai 10 hr 5 (Emirates); Istanbul 13 hr 10 (Turkish Airlines); Sydney 6 hr 30. US destinations: none listed.
dps_hub_routes.caveat: Aggregator schedule data; routes and carriers change by season. Says nothing about the US-to-hub leg, fares, or total journey time: those stay serve-live and must not be printed as figures.
dps_hub_routes.writing_rule: Name hub CITIES as examples of where a connection can be made; give the hub-to-Bali times as approximate and dated; never state a total door-to-door time or a fare.

dot_connections.value: The US Department of Transportation advises travelers booking a connection to check the time between flights and ask what happens if the first flight is delayed; to choose the least-congested connecting airport and consider weather when fares are equal; and, on a connection involving two airlines, to ask whether bags will be transferred. It ranks itineraries from safest for baggage to riskiest: nonstop, through flight, same-airline connection, connection between different airlines. On international itineraries passengers may be able to claim expenses caused by a delay under Article 19 of the Montreal Convention by filing a claim with the airline; for US domestic itineraries airlines are not required to compensate for delays or cancellations.
dot_connections.scope: air travelers from the United States
dot_connections.support: DOT 'Fly Rights', read directly in Chrome: 'When making your reservation for a connection, always check the amount of time between flights. Ask yourself what will happen if the first flight is delayed; if you don't like the answer, pick another flight or "construct" a connection that allows more time.' 'If you have a choice of connections and the fares and service are equivalent, choose the one with the least-congested connecting airport... You may wish to take into consideration the potential for adverse weather'. 'If you have a connection involving two airlines, ask whether your bags will be transferred.' Baggage ranking: '1) nonstop flight; 2) direct or through flight; 3) online connection (change of aircraft but not airlines); and 4) interline connection (change of aircraft and airlines)'. 'Contrary to popular belief, for domestic itineraries airlines are not required to compensate passengers whose flights are delayed or canceled.' 'On international itineraries, passengers may be able to recover reimbursement under Article 19 of the Montreal Convention for expenses resulting from a delayed or canceled flight by filing a claim with the airline.' 'if an early flight does get delayed or canceled, you have more rerouting options.'
dot_connections.caveat: Does not use the phrase 'separate tickets' and does not say what an airline does when a passenger on a separately booked onward flight misses it. Do not state airline behaviour; frame it as a question to ask.

domestic_baggage.value: Indonesian regulation sorts domestic airlines into three service groups. Under Transport Ministry Regulation PM 185 of 2015, a full-service airline includes up to 20 kg of checked baggage in an economy fare, a medium-service airline up to 15 kg, and a no-frills airline may charge for checked baggage.
domestic_baggage.scope: economy passengers on scheduled domestic flights in Indonesia
domestic_baggage.support: Search summaries of Indonesian legal and business press (Hukumonline, Kontan, Detik, Tirto) on Article 22 of PM 185/2015: three groups, 'full service', 'medium service', 'no frills'; 'recorded baggage is allowed up to a maximum of 20 kilograms' for full service, '15 kilograms' for medium service; 'no frills airlines can charge fees for recorded baggage'.
domestic_baggage.caveat: The regulation itself (jdih.dephub.go.id) could not be opened; this is press coverage read as search summaries. Later amendments not checked. Do not say which airline is in which group, and give no carry-on weights, change fees or refund rules: tell readers to read their fare's conditions.

_held_secondary._note: Not fact records. Sourced only at second hand on a high-stakes point. Never span these in an article.

when_to_go.nyepi_airport_closure.value: On Nyepi, Bali's airport stops all regular commercial flights for 24 hours, from 6 a.m. on the day itself to 6 a.m. the next morning. In 2026 that meant 06:00 on Thursday, March 19, to 06:00 on Friday, March 20, with 440 scheduled flights not operating; medical and specially authorised flights were still handled.
when_to_go.nyepi_airport_closure.scope: I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport on Nyepi; hours stated for 2026
when_to_go.nyepi_airport_closure.support: Tempo (English), 13 March 2026, read directly, quoting the airport's general manager: '"All regular commercial flight activities at the airport will be halted from Thursday, March 19, 2026, at 06:00 WITA (UTC+8) until Friday, March 20, 2026, at 06:00 WITA," said Nugroho Jati, General Manager of PT Angkasa Pura Indonesia (InJourney Airports) for I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport'. A detik report of the same announcement gives 440 flights (231 domestic, 209 international) and says the last international departure before closure was at 01:30.
when_to_go.nyepi_airport_closure.caveat: Secondary: a news report of the airport operator's statement, for 2026 only. No operator page was found. The 2027 hours are not announced; describe the pattern and tell readers to confirm with their airline.
when_to_go.nyepi_airport_closure.writing_rule: Articles may describe the closure in attributed prose ('in 2026 the airport's general manager announced a 24-hour halt from 6 a.m.') but must NOT put it in a fact span, and must tell readers to confirm their own flight with the airline.
when_to_go.nyepi_airport_closure.hold_reason: High-stakes and secondary-only, so the validator refuses it as a fact. The Transport Ministry published its own statement on 15 March 2026 ('Kemenhub Sesuaikan Operasional Transportasi Jelang Hari Raya Nyepi di Bali', dephub.go.id) but the ministry's firewall rejects requests from this network in both the terminal and Chrome; a newspaper republication of it (Suara Merdeka, 16 March 2026) was opened and confirms the statement exists. Promote this record once the ministry page or an airport-operator page can be read.

when_to_go.nyepi_stay_indoors.value: During Nyepi, residents and tourists alike are not permitted to travel or leave their accommodation, and fireworks, loudspeakers and other noise are prohibited, under the annual joint appeal issued by Bali's interfaith forum and provincial authorities.
when_to_go.nyepi_stay_indoors.support: Google's index of a detik report of the 2026 joint appeal (Seruan Bersama): 'Seluruh masyarakat dan wisatawan tidak diperkenankan bepergian/keluar rumah serta menyalakan petasan/mercon, pengeras suara, bunyi-bunyian'. The ministerial circular read directly refers to the same joint appeal by name and date (18 February 2026).
when_to_go.nyepi_stay_indoors.hold_reason: The joint appeal's own text was not opened; only a news report of it.
when_to_go.nyepi_stay_indoors.writing_rule: Describe in attributed prose, no fact span.

visa.arrival_card_contents.value: The All Indonesia arrival card is one digital form that combines the immigration, customs and health declarations, replacing the separate customs e-CD and SATUSEHAT health forms. Each traveler, including children, needs their own. It asks for passport and contact details, flight and accommodation, and health and customs questions, and the QR code is sent by email.
visa.arrival_card_contents.scope: all international passengers arriving in Indonesia
visa.arrival_card_contents.support: Delegate travel guide (Sept 2025) published by the World Organisation for Animal Health for a conference in Indonesia, PDF read page by page: 'a unified digital form that combines several previous arrival/declaration forms (immigration, customs, health, etc.) into one. The form replaces ... getting_around.boat_safety.value: Passenger boats between Sanur and Nusa Penida come under the harbor master's office, KSOP Benoa, which issues the sailing approval each boat needs before departure and has told operators not to send boats out when the weather is poor, pointing them to the meteorological agency's wave forecasts. Indonesia's state news agency reported that in May 2023 the agency forecast waves of 2.5 to 4 meters in the Badung Strait, which the Sanur to Nusa Penida route crosses, and that waves above 2.5 meters put such boats at risk. It also reported that on 5 August 2025 a fast boat arriving from Nusa Penida with 75 passengers and 5 crew capsized in the entrance channel to Sanur harbor when it was hit by a large wave; two foreign passengers died and a crew member was missing. The harbor master attributed it to natural conditions, with forecast waves of 2 to 4 meters, and said the boat was within its certified capacity of 75.
getting_around.boat_safety.scope: fast boats between Bali (Sanur) and the Nusa islands
getting_around.boat_safety.support: ANTARA (state news agency), 6 Aug 2025, read directly in Chrome: 'Kantor Kesyahbandaran dan Otoritas Pelabuhan (KSOP) Kelas II Benoa menyatakan kapal cepat ... tenggelam di jalur masuk Pelabuhan Sanur akibat faktor alam'; 'membawa 75 penumpang dan lima awak kapal dari Pelabuhan Nusa Penida tenggelam sekitar pukul 15.15 Wita'; 'terhantam ombak ... tergulung ombak jadi kapalnya langsung terbalik'; 'berdasarkan BMKG tinggi ombak berkisar 2-4 meter'; 'jumlah penumpang yang diizinkan sesuai sertifikasi kapal adalah 75'; 80 on board, 73 foreign nationals; (via fetch) two foreign nationals dead, one crew member missing, 77 survivors. ANTARA, 12 May 2023 (via fetch): KSOP Benoa's head of maritime safety: 'Jangan memaksa memberangkatkan kapal bila cuaca kurang bagus'; checks before the sailing approval (Surat Persetujuan Berlayar) is issued; BMKG waves 2.5-4 m in the Badung Strait; risk above 2.5 m; 64 fast boats on the route.
getting_around.boat_safety.caveat: A news agency's reports of the harbor authority's statements, not the authority's own page or a regulation (Transport Ministry site unreachable). The final casualty count of the 2025 accident was not re-checked after the first report: say 'two passengers died' as reported at the time. NEVER name the vessel or any operator. No cancellation rates, no refund rules, no claim that boats are 'safe' or 'unsafe' in general.
getting_around.boat_safety.writing_rule: HELD SECONDARY: describe only in attributed prose (travel guides / the state news agency / delegate guidance report ...), never in a fact span.

places.nusa_islands.value: Three islands lie off Bali's southeast coast. Nusa Penida is the largest, about 247 square km, with rough, hilly roads away from the north coast; its sights include Kelingking Beach, Angel's Billabong, Broken Beach, Crystal Bay, Atuh Beach and Diamond Beach, and Manta Point for diving. Nusa Lembongan is small, about 8 square km, with Jungutbatu village, Mushroom Bay, Dream Beach, Devil's Tear and a mangrove forest, and surfing, snorkeling and diving; a yellow suspension bridge for walkers and motorbikes links it to tiny Nusa Ceningan. Boats leave mainly from Sanur, with others from Padang Bai; guides give the Sanur crossing as roughly 30 to 45 minutes, and most Lembongan boats involve a wet landing, wading from the beach. Most visitors see Nusa Penida on a day trip, and accommodation exists along its north coast. Travel guides warn of strong rip currents at Dream Beach and of fatal falls at Devil's Tear. On Nusa Penida, travel guides describe the path to Kelingking Beach as a clifftop descent of about 400 meters, describe Peguyangan Spring as reached by about 700 stairs on a cliff edge, warn against swimming at Broken Beach at high tide because of waves, and warn of heat. Nusa Penida's arrival harbors are on the north coast (Toyapakeh, Buyuk, Sampalan), and Nusa Lembongan is about ten minutes from Nusa Penida by local boat.
places.nusa_islands.support: Wikivoyage Nusa Penida and Nusa Lembongan (via fetch): Penida 'the largest of three islands', 247 km2; speedboat from Sanur about 30 minutes, slower ferry from Padang Bai; harbours Toyapakeh, Buyuk, Sampalan, Banjar Nyuh; 'Roads in Nusa Penida are rough, hilly away from the north coast'; Peguyangan 700 stairs; most visitors on day cruises, accommodation between Toyapakeh and Sampalan. Lembongan about 8 km2; Sanur primary port, also Serangan, Padang Bai; 35-45 minutes; 'wet landings, with passengers wading knee-deep or higher'; yellow suspension bridge to Ceningan; Penida about 10 minutes by local boat; 'Be very careful though about entering the water' at Dream Beach (rip currents); Devil's Tear 'many tourists have fallen to their deaths here'; no personal cars.
places.nusa_islands.caveat: Boat crossing times are a travel wiki's figures, not an operator's or regulator's; give them as 'roughly' and tell readers to check with the operator. No boat safety or cancellation rules are sourced (Transport Ministry site unreachable). Never name a boat company.
places.nusa_islands.writing_rule: HELD SECONDARY: describe only in attributed prose (travel guides / the state news agency / delegate guidance report ...), never in a fact span.

places.gili_islands.value: The Gili Islands are three small islands off northwest Lombok: Gili Trawangan, the largest and known as the party island; Gili Air, the closest to Lombok, with an established local community; and Gili Meno, the quietest. There are no cars or motorbikes on any of them. From Bali they are reached by fast boat, with Padang Bai in East Bali the main port (a crossing of roughly an hour and a half), longer crossings from the south, and a shorter sea route from Amed; or by flying to Lombok's airport, then driving to the harbor area at Bangsal and taking a boat. Travel guides warn that fast boats are small high-speed craft, that crew training and safety standards vary, that sea conditions are roughest in July and August, and that travelers with concerns about a vessel, overloading or weather should not board.
places.gili_islands.support: Wikivoyage Gili Islands (via fetch): Trawangan 340 ha 'party island', Air 188 ha, Meno 150 ha 'most laid-back'; 'There are no cars or motorbikes to disturb the peace'; Padang Bai about 1.5 hours, Serangan about 2.5 hours, Amed 'Shortest sea route'; via Lombok International Airport then taxi about 1 h 40 to 2 h to Bangsal or Teluk Nare, then boat; fast boats 'smaller high speed craft with light duty hull construction'; 'Crew training and safety standards vary considerably'; 'If you have legitimate concerns about the vessel, operator, overloading, or weather conditions then do not board'; 'Sea conditions worsen July-August with strong swells'; night crossings not recommended.
places.gili_islands.caveat: Volunteer travel wiki; crossing times are its figures, not an operator's or regulator's. No official boat-safety or cancellation rules are sourced. Give times as 'roughly', attribute the warnings to travel guides, name no company, and never state how often boats are cancelled.
places.gili_islands.writing_rule: HELD SECONDARY: describe only in attributed prose (travel guides / the state news agency / delegate guidance report ...), never in a fact span.

places.batur.value: Mount Batur is an active volcano of about 1,700 meters in the Kintamani area, inside a large caldera with a crater lake, Lake Batur. Travel guides describe the sunrise climb as starting from the lakeside village of Toya Bungkah, taking about two hours to the summit, with more than half of the route through forest, and as requiring a guide from the local Association of Mount Batur Trekking Guides. The village has hot springs. Penelokan, on the caldera rim, is the main viewpoint, best early before cloud forms. Kintamani is usually much cooler than the coast, and a sweater or jacket is advised. Guides warn that touts target visitors and suggest booking the climb in advance.
places.batur.support: Wikivoyage Kintamani (via fetch): Batur 1,700 metres, 'still an active volcano'; caldera about 1,500 m; trek from Toya Bungkah 'about 2 hours', 'more than half of the climb is through pleasant shady forest'; guides mandatory, members of the Association of Mount Batur Trekking Guides, office in Toya Bungkah; hot springs; Penelokan 'spectacular views of this crater lake and Mount Batur', best early; Pura Ulun Danu Batur; 'usually about 15 degrees cooler than down on the coast'; 'a sweater or jacket advisable'; touts target visitors, pre-booking helps.
places.batur.caveat: Volunteer wiki. It calls the climb 'very easy': do NOT repeat a difficulty rating; say 'about two hours' and that it is a pre-dawn climb on a volcano. No start times, no prices. '15 degrees cooler' has no unit stated: say 'much cooler'. Volcanic activity status is not sourced: tell readers to check before booking.
places.batur.writing_rule: HELD SECONDARY: describe only in attributed prose (travel guides / the state news agency / delegate guidance report ...), never in a fact span.

unesco_subak.value: Bali's rice-terrace landscape is a UNESCO World Heritage site, inscribed in 2012 as the 'Cultural Landscape of Bali Province: the Subak System as a Manifestation of the Tri Hita Karana Philosophy'. It consists of five rice-terrace areas and their water temples covering 19,500 hectares. Subak is a cooperative water-management system of canals and weirs that dates back to the 9th century. The listing includes the 18th-century royal water temple Pura Taman Ayun, the water temple Pura Ulun Danu Batur on Lake Batur, and the subak landscape of the Pakerisan watershed.
unesco_subak.support: UNESCO World Heritage Centre page, read directly in Chrome: 'The cultural landscape of Bali consists of five rice terraces and their water temples that cover 19,500 ha. The temples are the focus of a cooperative water management system of canals and weirs, known as subak, that dates back to the 9th century. Included in the landscape is the 18th-century Royal Water Temple of Pura Taman Ayun'; 'Tri Hita Karana, which brings together the realms of the spirit, the human world and nature'; 'Date of Inscription: 2012'; sites include 'the Supreme Water Temple of Pura Ulun Danu Batur on the edge of Lake Batur' and 'the Subak Landscape of the Pakerisan Watershed the oldest known irrigation system in Bali'.
unesco_subak.caveat: The text read did not show the name Jatiluwih on screen (it is in the Catur Angga Batukaru component per UNESCO's fuller description, not re-read). Say 'the Jatiluwih terraces are widely described as part of the UNESCO-listed subak landscape' or omit the UNESCO link for Jatiluwih. Tegallalang is NOT established as part of the listing.

regions.value: Bali is about 144 km (89 miles) from east to west and 80 km (50 miles) north to south. Travel guides divide it into South Bali (Kuta, Legian, Seminyak, Canggu, Jimbaran, the Bukit peninsula, Nusa Dua, Sanur, Denpasar), Central Bali (Ubud, Bedugul, Tabanan), East Bali (Amed, Candidasa, Padang Bai, Sidemen, Kintamani, Mount Agung), North Bali (Lovina, Singaraja), West Bali (West Bali National Park, the ferry to Java) and the southeastern islands (Nusa Lembongan, Nusa Ceningan, Nusa Penida).

ubud.value: Ubud is a town in central Bali, at about 200 meters above sea level, cooler than the coast, and regarded as the island's cultural and arts center. It is made up of fourteen villages, each with its own village committee (banjar). The center has three main streets, Jalan Raya Ubud, Jalan Monkey Forest and Jalan Hanoman, meeting near the market and the palace. Surrounding villages include Campuhan, Sanggingan and Penestanan to the north and west, Nyuh Kuning and Pengosekan to the south, and Peliatan to the east. Sights include the Ubud market and palace, the Sacred Monkey Forest, the Campuhan ridge walk, Goa Gajah to the east, Tirta Empul to the north, and the Tegallalang rice terraces about 9 km to the northeast. Central Ubud is walkable and congested with traffic.
ubud.support: Wikivoyage Ubud (via fetch): elevation about 200 m, 'cooler temperatures than the coast'; 'fourteen villages, each run by its own banjar'; three main streets Jl Raya Ubud, Jl Monkey Forest, Jl Hanoman; villages listed by direction; Goa Gajah about one hour's walk east; Tirta Empul 15-18 km north; Tegallalang 9 km; 'Central Ubud is overrun with tourists and touts, and traffic is terrible.'

east_and_north.value: East Bali in travel-guide terms: Amed is a strip of quiet fishing villages with black sand beaches, coral reefs and diving; Tulamben is known for diving the USAT Liberty shipwreck; Candidasa is a quiet coastal town; Padang Bai is a small port town where ferries to Lombok leave, with white sand coves; Sidemen is a valley of rice terraces and forested hills with easy walks; Tirta Gangga is a water palace; Pura Besakih, on the slopes of Mount Agung, is regarded by Balinese Hindus as their mother temple; Mount Agung is the island's highest mountain; Kintamani has the active volcano Mount Batur, described as about a two-hour climb. North Bali: Lovina is a string of quiet villages with black sand beaches, known for dawn boat trips to see dolphins; Singaraja is the largest town on the north coast and the former colonial capital; Sekumpul is a group of waterfalls in a jungle valley. Bedugul, in the central mountains, has lakes, a botanical garden and the Ulun Danu Bratan temple.
east_and_north.support: Wikivoyage East Bali, North Bali and Bali pages (via fetch): Amed 'peaceful, traditional fishing villages featuring black sand beaches, coral reefs and excellent diving'; Tulamben USAT Liberty wreck; Candidasa 'a quiet coastal town'; Padang Bai 'small port town from where ferries to Lombok depart'; Sidemen 'one of the most scenic drives on the whole island', 'undemanding hikes'; Tirta Gangga water palace; 'Pura Besakih is considered by the Hindu Balinese to be their mother temple'; Agung 'the highest mountain on the island'; Batur 'an easy two-hour climb'; Lovina 'Quiet coastal villages with black sand beaches', dawn dolphin trips; Singaraja 'largest town on the north coast and the former administrative capital'; Sekumpul 'several waterfalls cascading side by side'; Bedugul 'pretty lakes in the mountains, a golf course, the botanical gardens and the famous Ulun Danu Bratan Temple'.

Munduk and Lempuyang are NOT described in the pages read: say only where they are (distances record) unless sourced separately. No claims about how hard a climb is beyond the quoted 'about two hours' for Batur.

munduk.value: Munduk is a village in the western highlands of central Bali, in the wider Bedugul area, at over 700 meters of altitude, where the climate is distinctly cool. Travel guides describe it as known for waterfalls, coffee and clove plantations, trekking, and the nearby twin crater lakes of Buyan and Tamblingan, with the Ulun Danu Bratan temple on Lake Bratan in the same highlands. It is about 20 km from Lovina on the north coast, and suits travelers who want nature, walking and cooler air. Travel guides call Munduk Waterfall perhaps the most impressive accessible falls on the island, powerful in the wet season.
munduk.support: Wikivoyage Munduk/Bedugul (via fetch): 'village in the mountain range of Central Bali'; elevations exceeding 700 metres, 'the tallest mountain peaking above 2,000 metres'; Munduk Waterfall 'perhaps the most impressive accessible falls on the whole island'; 'clove trees everywhere at the side of the highland roads'; twin lakes Buyan and Tamblingan; Pura Ulun Danu Bratan; about 20 km from Lovina; suits nature enthusiasts and trekkers.
munduk.caveat: Volunteer travel wiki. No temperatures, no trail lengths or difficulty, no waterfall entrance fees.

amed.value: Amed is a coastal strip in East Bali running about 14 km east from Culik through seven villages, including Jemeluk, Bunutan, Lipah and Selang. Travel guides describe it as a diving and snorkeling area with coral reefs close to shore, a shallow Japanese shipwreck, traditional salt making, black and grey sand and pebble beaches lined with outrigger fishing boats, and views of Mount Agung. The USAT Liberty wreck, a US Army transport ship torpedoed in 1942, lies at Tulamben up the coast. The Tirta Gangga water palace is a day trip. Local public transport is limited.
amed.support: Wikivoyage Amed (via fetch): 'stretching approximately 14 km eastward from Culik', seven villages 'Amed, Jemeluk, Bunutan, Lipah, Selang, Banyuning, and Aas'; USAT Liberty 'a US Army transport ship torpedoed by a Japanese submarine in 1942' at Tulamben; Japanese wreck at Banyuning in shallow water; salt production; views of Mount Agung; 'Black pebble and grey-brown sandy beaches'; public transport limited, car with driver recommended; a fast-boat service links Amed with the Gili Islands; suits divers, snorkellers and relaxed coastal holidays.
amed.caveat: Volunteer travel wiki. The page's taxi time and prices are NOT to be used. Never name a boat company. Dive-site difficulty and depths are not sourced.

tanah_lot_lempuyang.value: Tanah Lot is a sea temple on a rock just offshore on Bali's southwest coast, one of the island's important directional temples, attributed to the 15th-century priest Nirartha; travel guides describe the area as very busy in the late afternoon before sunset, with the approach lined by souvenir shops. Pura Lempuyang is a temple high in the mountains of Karangasem in East Bali, famous for the 'Gates of Heaven' photograph; travel writers report a numbered queue for the photo that can run to hours, and that the reflection seen in the famous picture is made by a photographer holding a mirror under the phone, not by water. Gunung Kawi, an 11th-century site near Ubud, is reached by climbing down 371 steps; Tirta Empul is a 10th-century spring temple used for ritual purification; Goa Gajah is an 11th-century cave with a carved demon's mouth at its entrance.
tanah_lot_lempuyang.support: Wikivoyage Tanah Lot (via fetch): 'a coastal temple in South Bali' on an offshore rock, 'one of the important directional temples in Bali', Nirartha, 15th century; 'often very busy indeed, especially in the late afternoons, pre-sunset'; 'a maze of souvenir shops'. No entrance fees or opening hours for any site. Whether visitors may enter Tanah Lot's temple itself is not sourced; the governor's circular (culture.temple_access) is the rule to cite.

waterfalls.value: Waterfalls named by Bali travel guides include Tegenungan, near Ubud, about 30 meters high and described as easy to reach; Tibumana, east of Ubud, a short walk from its parking area; Tukad Cepung, partly hidden in a cave-like canyon and known for light beams; Kanto Lampo, where visitors wade through water for photographs; Nungnung, in a jungle ravine north of Denpasar, reached by about 500 stone steps; and, in the north, Gitgit, Banyumala twin falls near Wanagiri, Munduk Waterfall, and Sekumpul, a group of falls in a jungle valley.
waterfalls.support: Search-result summaries of several travel pages (World of Waterfalls, Honeycombers, Contiki and others) agreeing on: Tegenungan 'around 30m high', 'Access to Tegenungan is easy'; Tibumana '5-minute walk from the parking'; Tukad Cepung 'partially hidden within a cave-like canyon where sunlight pours through'; Kanto Lampo 'walk through waist-deep water'; Nungnung '45km north of Denpasar', '500 stone steps'; Banyumala 'twin waterfall located in Wanagiri Hills Sukasada Buleleng'; Gitgit in the north, easy to reach. waterfalls.caveat: Travel blogs read as search summaries. No entrance fees, no swimming-safety claims, no flow or flash-flood claims. Step counts only where quoted (Nungnung about 500).

manta_rays.value: Manta rays are seen in the waters off Nusa Penida, at sites known as Manta Point and Manta Bay, which researchers describe as shallow reefs used year-round by manta rays and frequently visited by tourism operators. Indonesia gave manta rays full legal protection in 2014 under a decree of the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries, and Nusa Penida's waters are one of the country's designated manta sanctuaries.
manta_rays.support: Search summaries of a 2019 Frontiers in Marine Science paper and conservation-group releases (WCS, WWF, Mongabay): 'Decree Number 4/KEPMEN-KP/2014 ... two manta ray species ... full protection throughout their entire life cycle'; 'three manta ray sanctuaries were established in Raja Ampat, West Manggarai including Komodo National Park, and Nusa Penida (200 km2)'; 'Year-round records were collected from two shallow (<20 m) reefs - Manta Bay and Manta Point - that are used frequently by tourism operators'; sites include cleaning stations and feeding areas.
manta_rays.caveat: Read as search summaries, not full text. No sighting odds, no season claims, no claims about sea conditions at the sites. Do not name operators.

balinese_dishes.value: Balinese cooking is built on pork, chicken, duck, seafood and vegetables, seasoned with a spice paste (base genep or basa gede) of garlic, shallots, chilies, ginger, turmeric, palm sugar and shrimp paste. Pork is central, which sets it apart from the rest of mostly Muslim Indonesia; beef is rarely eaten because of Hindu tradition. Well-known dishes: babi guling, spit-roasted suckling pig stuffed with chili, turmeric, garlic and ginger; bebek betutu and ayam betutu, duck or chicken heavily seasoned, wrapped in leaves and slow-cooked; lawar, a mix of chopped vegetables such as young jackfruit with coconut, minced meat and pork rind, of which the red version contains fresh pig's blood; sate lilit, spiced minced meat pressed around a lemongrass stick; nasi campur Bali, rice with several small portions of meat, fish, tofu, tempeh and vegetables; sambal matah, a raw relish of shallots, chili, lemongrass and lime in coconut oil; urutan, a pork sausage; jukut urab, vegetables with grated coconut; laklak, small rice-flour pancakes with coconut and palm sugar; bubuh injin, black sticky rice pudding. Peanuts appear in sauces, and coconut milk is widely used. Brem is a rice wine.
balinese_dishes.support: Wikipedia 'Balinese cuisine' (via fetch): babi guling 'roasted suckling pig' stuffed with chili, turmeric, garlic, ginger; betutu 'steamed or roasted poultry (chicken or duck) highly seasoned', wrapped in banana leaves; lawar with 'shredded unripe jackfruit, young banana flower', pork rind, 'can contain raw pig blood', white and red varieties; sate lilit 'spiced minced meat on a stick' on lemongrass; nasi campur Bali; basa gede 'garlic, red chilies, shallots, nutmeg, ginger, turmeric, palm sugar, cumin, shrimp paste'; sambal matah; 'beef is never or rarely consumed'; shrimp paste, coconut milk, peanuts (in sauces), chilies; urutan, jukut urab, laklak, bubuh injin, brem.
balinese_dishes.caveat: An encyclopedia summary. Ingredients vary by cook: never tell a reader with an allergy that a dish is free of something. No restaurant names, no prices.
